I enjoyed many subreddits that required verification of an advanced degree to receive specialized flair. I have my undergraduate in Neuromuscular Physiology with a minor (soon to be major after grad school) in Biochemistry. I'm about to begin my third year of Physical Therapy School here at Texas State, in my opinion it helps to see someone truly has the knowledge and understanding to support their claims. Is there some sort of implementation of that concept here? If not is it something others feel we should do?

I talked with the /r/fitness mods a lot about this, I'm guessing you are looking at something like /r/askhistorians flairs or /r/weightroom flair. There are a few problems with implementing it:

  1. Work, let's face it specialized flair is good but you would not only have to give it to people with degrees but also to people that might not have a degree but are either strong, fast, athletic etc.

  2. Which ones do you give it to? There are more relevant degrees but what if someone wants flair for biochem because of supplements. What about doctors? This could make some people and fields really angry and is a potential drama mine.

  3. Dogma, this was one of the big concerns, reddit has a problem with worshipping science to an absurd amount (Engineer/Biologist/Jackdawist here). Now in theory this is no problem so long as the person with flair isn't saying anything wrong, however if they do they are less likely to be called on it, should the flair just be revoked in such a case? What if he claims it was just a mistake? How many mistakes can a person make until they don't have special privilege anymore.

In the end I think flairs can work and can improve a community but I have to agree with the fittit mods that there will be a lot of work and drama coming with it.
